properties.name: A design can be asked what fraction of any declared kind of thing carries a given relation — without somebody writing a script
properties.statement:
Anthony's word, 2026-08-31, promoted from the session's own evidence. STATED AS A PROPERTY, NOT A DESIGN — how it is served is not settled here.

THE PROPERTY: a reader can ask this design "of my N things of kind X, how many carry relation R?" and get an answer, for any X and R the schema declares — not only for the handful somebody has already hardcoded.

📌 DISTINCT FROM `fact:five-capabilities-...-one-query-shape-found-them-all`, having read it: that node MEASURES what one session found and how (five instances, all hand-rolled). This states what must stay TRUE of the product. Recording what was observed and recording what is now required are different acts on the same work, and the fact is the evidence for this requirement rather than a restatement of it.

═══ WHY IT IS A REQUIREMENT AND NOT A CONVENIENCE ═══
It is the core traceability question of systems engineering, in the user's own words rather than reflow2's: HOW MANY OF MY REQUIREMENTS ARE ACTUALLY VERIFIED? How many of my components have a declared interface? How many of my capabilities have anything that consumes them? A design tool that cannot answer that on demand asks the user to trust a coverage claim it cannot show its working for.

═══ THE EVIDENCE, MEASURED 2026-08-31 ═══
Five separate findings in ONE session came from exactly this question, and every one was answered by an ad-hoc script over the committed export because no served read does it:
    3 of 22 Interfaces carry an incoming VERIFIES
    3 of 192 Capabilities carry a signature
    3 of 45 struct-coupled modules sit behind the read trait
    20 of 181 Capabilities have a recorded consumer
    3 of 4 Constraints are budgets
`find_tools` on "count edges of one type pointing at nodes of another type" returns a node lister and two bulk WRITERS. Also filed as a `report_manual_work` with diagnosis `tool_missing`.

⭐ FOUR SPECIAL CASES OF THIS SHAPE ALREADY EXIST, WHICH IS THE ARGUMENT. `coverage_report`, `consumption_report`, `seam_coverage` and the delivery line each answer ONE fixed pair, well. That four were built separately says the shape is wanted repeatedly; it also means every new pair needs a new tool and a new release.

🛑 AND THE NEAR-MISS IS WHAT MAKES IT SHARP. `vocabulary_coverage` answers this at TYPE level — is this node type, edge type or property ever used — and on 2026-08-31 it scored the `functional` domain 1.0 on both node and edge types while `set_capability_signature` sat at 3 of 192. USED ONCE AND USED EVERYWHERE IT APPLIES ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE TO A TYPE-LEVEL READING. Instance-level coverage is a different question and the design does not hold it.

═══ ⚠️ WHAT THIS REQUIREMENT MUST NOT BE READ AS ═══
· NOT a claim that low coverage is a DEFECT. A capability built ahead of its consumer, a deliberate extension point and genuine surplus all produce the same fraction — the caution `consumption_report` already states about itself. The requirement is that the number be ASKABLE, never that it be high.
· NOT a request for a verdict or a score. `dec:report-dont-judge` governs the neighbourhood and should govern this.
· NOT settled as to surface. Whether it is one general tool, a parameterised report or a query language is open — and a general form has a cost the four special cases do not: each of those carries domain-specific bounds and `not_observed_about` prose that a generic answer would lose.
